questions.question: Name four ways to make paper stronger.
questions.expected_answer: Folding it, for example into a concertina or zigzag, rolling it into tubes, layering several sheets by gluing them together, and corrugating it with a wavy layer between flat sheets.

questions.question: Explain why a folded concertina bridge holds more coins than a flat sheet.
questions.expected_answer: The folds stand up like little walls running along the bridge, so the paper becomes stiff along its length and does not sag. A flat sheet is thin and has nothing to stop it bending.

questions.question: What makes the paper bridge test a fair test?
questions.expected_answer: Every group uses the same size sheet of paper, the same gap between the books and the same kind of coins, added one at a time in the middle. Only the way the paper is shaped is changed.
